unit.why: A short anecdote: a poor jester, provoked by his wife, comes to R. Pinchas, who advises him to stop jesting so that he will have a livelihood. The compiler then adds a long homiletic and talmudic elaboration and a footnote.
unit.boundary_note: The division mixes the story with the compiler's homiletic footnotes. A displaced footnote fragment ('להם הלחם. והטעם כי]...') continues text from elsewhere, and the last footnote breaks off at 'בא', continuing past this division.

stories.start_quote: שפ"א הי' איש בדחן שהרבה מאד
stories.end_quote: ויהי' לך שריד לאוכלך עכ״ל ודפח"ח
stories.summary_en: A poor jester whose wife berates him for lack of food comes angrily to R. Pinchas, who tells him to stop his jesting, because a person's allotted measure of pleasure is fixed each Rosh Hashana and he is spending it on jokes instead of bread.
